ruleName: Actions That Improve Conditions Affecting the Stroke
title: Practice Swing in Long Rough – Improving Conditions Affecting the Stroke
question: Your ball is lying in long rough. Before playing your shot, you take a practice swing that knocks down some of the long grass directly behind the ball, making your next swing easier. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: There is no penalty because it was only a practice swing.
There is no penalty because you did not move the ball.
You receive the general penalty because you improved the conditions affecting your stroke.

explanation: You are allowed to take practice swings, but you must not improve the conditions affecting your stroke. If your practice swing deliberately or accidentally knocks down long grass directly behind the ball, improving your next swing, you receive the general penalty for improving the conditions affecting your stroke. See Rule 8.1a.
